SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Position and Directions Suggested vocabulary left, right, behind, in front, up,  in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to pronounce words correctly? 2) Why should you give god directions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy- as the learner uses new words in relevant contexts to talk about position and direction.

Values:
Respect as learners values the contribution of peers during dialogues.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (effective communication) as the learner gives and responds to simple specific two- directional instructions.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Correct pronunciation and vocabulary is emphasized in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.
